display.purpose: Hero headings, section titles, watermarks. DM Serif Display only.

headline.purpose: Sub-section headings, card headings. Bricolage Grotesque.

title.purpose: Card titles, named list items. Bricolage Grotesque.

body.purpose: All prose copy. Instrument Sans. Max 65–75ch.

label.purpose: Eyebrow labels, form field labels. Uppercase. Instrument Sans Bold.

shadows.name: clay
shadows.purpose: Cards and passive containers at rest.

shadows.name: clay-hover
shadows.purpose: Clay card on hover, paired with translateY(-3px).

shadows.name: neo-shadow
shadows.purpose: Buttons and interactive chips at rest. Hard, no blur.

shadows.name: neo-shadow-press
shadows.purpose: Button pressed state. Paired with translate(2px,2px) — offset must equal shadow reduction exactly.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for GSAP entrances and scroll-triggered reveals.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Button and link state transitions (hover, focus). 0.15s duration.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All durations collapse to this under prefers-reduced-motion. Elements revealed immediately.

narrative.overview:
This system is a cultural gazette that learned to build websites. It inherits the editorial warmth of small-press publishing — composed layouts, typographic authority, unhurried rhythm — and applies that sensibility to digital craft. The palette is terracotta, earth, and cream: not a metaphor for Cuenca, but the actual soil under it. The grain texture at opacity 0.025 isn't decoration; it is the surface.

Neo-brutalist structure anchors the interactive layer: hard 4px shadows on buttons press and shift like a physical stamp. Soft clay shadows on resting cards recall worn leather bindings. The tension between those two shadow modes — the stamp and the clay — is where the personality lives. Neither is decorative. Both communicate state and surface type.

This system explicitly rejects: flashy scroll experiments, SaaS startup aesthetics, overdesigned hero sections that perform creativity, and anything generic enough to belong to a template agency.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial over promotional — layouts breathe; information is not crammed
Tactile surfaces — two distinct shadow modes (stamp vs. clay) communicate surface type
Typography carries the weight — DM Serif Display is the prestige voice; Bricolage Grotesque is the working voice
Terracotta palette, light mode only — warmth is the project's geography, not a mood board choice
Accessibility is structural — #8B3A1E for all text on light; never #E8724A

rules.name: The Orange Two-Face Rule
rules.body: #E8724A and #8B3A1E are the same conceptual color at different contrast levels. Use #E8724A only when decorative. Use #8B3A1E the moment any text needs to be read.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: The body::after SVG noise overlay at opacity 0.025 is always present. It is part of the surface. Never build component previews without it.

rules.name: The Display Monopoly Rule
rules.body: DM Serif Display belongs to headings and decorative display text only. Navigation, captions, labels, and body copy are prohibited.

rules.name: The Italic Signal Rule
rules.body: Italic is a Cuencan Press editorial device — it marks the human moment inside a statement. Reserve for deliberate rhetorical emphasis; never for decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Clay and neo-shadow coexist, never on the same element. If it is an action (button, chip), it is neo. If it is a content container (card, panel), it is clay.

dos: Do use --orange-accessible (#8B3A1E) for any orange text on light backgrounds, at any size.
Do apply the full neo-shadow press: translate(2px,2px) reduces the shadow offset by exactly 2px in both directions.
Do include both clay shadow vectors — the counter-shadow is what lifts the card.
Do use not-italic on <em> inside display headings.
Do check prefers-reduced-motion in every GSAP animation and reveal elements immediately when set.
Do use clamp() for all section spacing and heading sizes.
Do use <a className={cn(buttonVariants({...}))}>  for anchor CTAs.
Do use Sienna Ink for focus rings on light backgrounds.
donts: Don't use #E8724A for any functional text on light backgrounds. It fails WCAG AA at 2.9:1.
Don't activate dark mode. .dark tokens are not in use.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't build overdesigned hero sections: no particle fields, no large 3D objects, no scroll-jacking for spectacle.
Don't use SaaS startup aesthetics — blue gradient backgrounds, floating 3D shapes, purple/teal schemes.
Don't use flashy scroll-driven animation for show.
Don't use Tailwind opacity or transform classes as GSAP initial state.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use --orange-soft (#F2A47C) on light cream backgrounds for text.
Don't use rem or fixed px for section-level vertical spacing — clamp() only.
